ElementTree and openpyxl are namespace-aware and order-tolerant, so the gap between them and Excel is silent by construction: the zip was intact, every part parsed, every relationship resolved, every style index was in range, and 391 controls passed on a workbook nobody could open. Isolated by bisecting the package, not by guessing. The original rows under a rebuilt header open; a rebuilt file under the original header does not. sheetData was never implicated.

The main namespace is registered as the default, the five header elements are assembled in the order the schema fixes, and attributes from other namespaces are dropped. x14ac:dyDescent is the only thing removed from the file, a text baseline hint whose prefix Excel declares at the worksheet root and which did not travel with the element. Nothing in the sheet moved: sheetData is byte for byte identical at 302,501 bytes, styles.xml and the theme and sharedStrings are unchanged, and two independent readers over all 5,544 cells found no value changed, no empty cell populated, no populated cell emptied, and 230 of 230 row digests matching. All 212 decisions, the 9 marked rows, the frozen pane and the ten column widths survived. The workbook had been unopenable since 2026-08-12, so this predates the move between machines rather than being caused by it.
